Taxonomic classification of the most complete bins with GTDB-Tk. Commands for this step were run in `gtdbtk/`.

## **Step 6: Perform taxonomic classification with gtdbtk**

Move into the `gtdbtk` folder

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/gtdbtk
```

The `genomes` subfolder holds a copyof each top bin (completeness above 15%) from step 5, which is the input for the gtdbtk.

Build the copy comand up in steps. First i checked that the loop could read the bin names from `bbd_topbins.txt`

```{bash}
while read bin;do echo $bin;done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

Turned each bin name into the path of its fasta file by adding the folder `../metabat/bins_bbd/` at the start and `.fa` at the end

```{bash}
while read bin;do echo "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa";done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

Then copied each bin into `genomes`, and listed the folder to check there was one file per bin

```{bash}
while read bin;do cp "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa" genomes;done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

Check that it worked by listing files within the `genomes` directory. There should be one file for each of the bins

```{bash}
ls genomes
```

Made a shell script, [run_gtdbtk.sh](gtdbtk/run_gtdbtk.sh), and saved it in `gtdbtk`

Submitted the job. It ran for about 60 minutes (just a guess as i submitted it and left it over night to run)

```{bash}
sbatch run_gtdbtk.sh
```

When it finished, I checked that it had produced the summary of classifications. The file was created, so the job worked

```{bash}
ls -l out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv
```

Copied the summary up into the `gtdbtk` folder. Git ignores everything inside `out`, but it can see a `.tsv` saved directly in `gtdbtk`, so this lets me add the summary to the repository

```{bash}
cp out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv .
```
